name: Unknown Base account module unauthenticated execute drains vault
summary: Account 0xc851e5a0 is an EIP-1167 clone of a router that resolves its logic through a registry to module 0xa2362ea5. That module's ERC725X-style execute(uint256,address,uint256,bytes) performs the call for any caller. Vault 0x36057cb0 lets 0xc851e5a0 withdraw. An attacker's constructor had the account call the vault's withdraw (0xaaa18f86) with itself as recipient and took 300,000 USDC. A second actor repeated the call nine days later and took 100,000 USDC.
notes: The registry already resolved module key 0xa487ef877067ccd6a14bb3575c193d40fdd5e6e7654313c354dedbaf3340f89a to 0xa2362ea5 (only event: block 40383887) when the account clone was created with that registry and key in its router slots; both slots and the registry answer are unchanged at block 45258485. execute() is open from the account's creation. The vault's later authorization of this account only set exposure.

Exact USDC debits from vault 0x36057cb08b7c19d8368bcad987484db8184145f6 through the open account execute: 300,000 USDC in source-1 (attacker 0xcccc6400) and 100,000 USDC in source-3 (second actor 0x359e11ab, 2026-05-06). No attacker input is involved. Native USDC on Base is valued at par.

The module, router, registry and vault have no verified source; the missing caller check is established from the struct-log trace of the module frame and from eth_call from an unrelated address, not from source text.
